title: Name the holding checkout on a reservation conflict
intent: Leases are control-plane: control_root_for (leases.rs:98-162) resolves every checkout's lease directory to the MAIN store, so main and every worktree share one lease dir. conflict_out (reserve.rs:439-455) prints only agent and cell, so a refusal cannot say which checkout holds the file — the cross-worktree FOREIGN_HOLD refusal already names its holder, this one goes blind. Reporting only: the conflict rule itself does not change.
action: In packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/reservations/: (1) reserve.rs — write a `holder` field onto the path lease record built at :256-271. The value is already in scope: roots.hold_topology() is called unconditionally at :51 and its holder string is the same one the cross-worktree hold row already carries at :331 ("main" for an ordinary checkout, the git-verified worktree id for a granted linked worktree). hold_topology() returns None for an UNGRANTED linked worktree — in that case write no holder field at all rather than inventing one. (2) leases.rs — carry holder on the Resv struct (:217-225), read it in lease_to_reservation (:227-266) with the same Option-and-omit pattern every other optional field uses, and emit it in resv_to_value (:271-296) only when present. (3) reserve.rs conflict_out (:439-455) — when a conflicting reservation carries a holder, the line reads `- <holder> holds "<path>" (cell <cell>, agent <agent>)`; with no holder it stays byte-for-byte as today. Do NOT change find_conflicts, is_hard_conflict, paths_overlap or any release/sweep scoping — this cell adds a reported fact, never a decision input. Leave lease_store.rs's generic acquire_leases writer (:534-544) alone; the integration-queue processor lease has no checkout to report.
acceptance: A reserve from an ordinary checkout writes holder "main" on the lease record; a reserve from a granted linked worktree writes its git-verified worktree id — proven over the real `git worktree add` fixtures already in tests.rs (:392-604).
A reserve from an UNGRANTED linked worktree writes no holder field at all, and every reader still parses that record.
A conflicting reserve's refusal text names the holding checkout, and the JSON conflicts[] entries carry holder.
A lease file written before this change (no holder key) is still read, listed, released and swept unchanged — proven by a fixture record with the field absent.
find_conflicts, is_hard_conflict and release scoping are untouched: the pre-existing conflict, release and sweep tests pass without modification.

truths: A path lease record carries holder "main" from an ordinary checkout and the git-verified worktree id from a granted worktree; an ungranted linked worktree writes no holder at all.
A reservation conflict refusal names the holding checkout in both the text lines and the JSON conflicts[].
A pre-existing lease record with no holder key still parses, lists, releases and sweeps.
Conflict detection and release scoping are byte-for-byte unchanged.
